The page opens on your plan and its one main action, for example Upgrade to Pro on Starter. A move up starts today and you pay the difference for the rest of the period. A move down takes effect at the end of the period you have paid for.

One control on that page opens the Stripe billing portal: Invoices and card details, in the Payment and invoices section. Payment method, billing address, tax IDs and the full invoice history are all there. Invoices are also reachable from the Invoices row in the settings menu, which opens the same portal.

articles.title: Invite your team and choose what each person can do
articles.summary: Add colleagues, give each person the right role (Admin, Manager, Viewer or Billing-Only), and manage your seats.
articles.html:
Who this is for

The owner or an admin of an organisation. A bid is easier with help, so you can invite colleagues and choose what each person can see and change. People you invite use the seats your plan includes.

The roles

Role What they can do
Owner Everything, including transferring ownership. There is one owner.
Admin Everything a Manager can do, plus inviting, changing roles for and removing members, and managing billing, plans and organisation settings.
Manager Full day to day work: create and edit bids, answers, requirements and reports, draft answers, run evaluations and export. Cannot manage the team, billing or settings.
Viewer Reads everything, comments on answers and records an approve, changes requested or reject decision on a bid. Cannot create, edit, export or delete.
Billing-Only Manages plans, payment methods and invoices, with no access to bids or reports.

The page also shows a full list of what each role can do, under What each role can do.

Step by step

  1. Open Settings, then Members & access.
  2. Under Invite a team member, enter one email address, or several separated by commas or new lines.
  3. Choose a role and select Send invite. For your security you may be asked for a fresh code from your authenticator first.

What happens next

Each person gets an email invitation and shows as Invite pending, with the time left before it expires. When they accept, they appear as Active. To change the role of a pending invitation, revoke it and invite again. To take someone off the team, choose Remove. They lose access straight away.

Common problems

  • Seat limit reached. All your seats are in use. Remove a member, or upgrade or add seats on the Billing page.
  • Already a member. That address already belongs to the team or has a pending invitation.
  • Someone outside your organisation needs to read one bid. Invite them as an external reviewer on that bid’s Sign-off stage instead. Your plan lists how many guest reviewers it includes.

articles.title: Security baselines, MFA enforcement, recovery codes & data controls
articles.summary: Turn on two-factor authentication, add a passkey, keep your recovery codes safe, set sign-in rules for your organisation and download a copy of your data.
articles.html:
Who this is for

Everyone with an account. Bids hold prices, plans and staff details a competitor would like to see, so a few minutes here protects your work. The organisation rules further down are for the owner or an admin.

Protect your own account

Open Settings, then Sign-in & security. It lists your password, two-factor authentication, passkeys, recovery codes, trusted devices and active sessions.

  1. Turn on two-factor authentication. Choose Enable two-factor authentication, scan the QR code with an authenticator app such as Google Authenticator, 1Password or Authy, then enter the 6-digit code. It is required for the Owner and Admin roles.
  2. Save your recovery codes somewhere safe. Each code works once, and they let you in if you lose your phone.
  3. Add a passkey if you like, so you sign in with your face, fingerprint or screen lock instead of typing a password.
  4. Check your active sessions and sign out any device you do not recognise.

Set rules for your organisation

Owners and admins open Authentication in the Organisation part of Settings. The organisation security policy can:

  • require two-factor authentication for every member,
  • set a minimum password length and the character types a password needs,
  • sign members out after a period of inactivity, from 15 minutes up to 7 days,
  • turn off the 30 day “Remember me” sign-in.

The same page holds an IP allowlist, which limits access to the addresses you approve, and says whether your plan includes it. Single sign-on is there too, for organisations that sign in with Microsoft, Google or Okta.

Get a copy of your data

In Preferences & privacy, choose Go to Your data, then Request export. You confirm it is you with your second factor first. We prepare a full copy of the records we hold on your account and email you a private download link, usually within a few minutes. The export history shows each request and when its link expires.

Common problems

  • Lost your authenticator? Sign in with a recovery code. If you have lost the codes too, Sign-in & security explains how to reset two-factor authentication.
  • Asked to verify again? Some actions, such as inviting a colleague or exporting data, ask for a fresh code from your authenticator first. Enter it and carry on.
  • Few recovery codes left? Regenerate a fresh set so you are not locked out.

articles.title: See who did what in the audit log
articles.summary: See sign-ins, team changes, billing changes and bid activity in one record, filter it, and export a copy for your own files.
articles.html:
What the audit log is for

The audit log records who did what, and when, across your organisation. It helps when a buyer or your insurer asks how you control access to your data, when you need to check who changed a bid, or when something looks wrong and you want to see what happened.

What it records

  • Sign-in and security: sign-ins, failed sign-ins, two-factor authentication turned on or off, passkeys added, password changes and sessions signed out.
  • Your team: invitations sent, accepted and revoked, role changes, members removed and ownership transferred.
  • Billing: plan changes, payments and cancellations.
  • Bids: tender documents added or removed, requirements confirmed or changed, compliance matrix updates and evidence removed.
  • Your data: requests for a copy of personal data, and account or organisation deletions.

Step by step

  1. Open Settings, then Audit log in the Organisation part. Owners and admins can see it.
  2. Filter by Action, by User and by date with From and To.
  3. Choose View on any row to see the full detail, including the request ID.
  4. Choose Export CSV or Export JSON to download the events that match your filters.

Times are shown in UTC, and the newest events come first.

Keeping your own copy

We keep this record for 24 months from the date of each event. If you need it for longer, for example for a contract that runs several years, export a copy and keep it in your own files.

Common problems

  • No events match these filters. Try a wider date range, or clear the action and user filters.
  • The export holds only the most recent events. Very large exports are capped. Narrow the date range and export again to reach older events.
  • We couldn’t load the audit log. This is a loading problem, not an empty log. Choose Refresh to try again.

articles.title: How to get help, report a problem or book a call
articles.summary: Choose the quickest way to get help, see when our team is available, and report a problem so it can be fixed fast.
articles.html:
Four ways to get help

Open Help and support from the menu. Pick the route that suits your question.

Route Best for When
AI support assistant How to questions and quick answers about Velstrian Tenderworks, procurement and social value. Any time it shows as available.
Report an issue Something that is not working. Any time. You get a reference straight away.
Email us at contact@velstrian.com Account, billing and detailed questions. We’ll reply by email, usually within one business day.
Book a call A walkthrough or a longer conversation. A 30 minute call at a time you choose.

Asking the assistant

Select Help and support (the lifebuoy icon) in the top bar, or Help in the menu on a phone, then Ask the AI support assistant. General questions are answered without using your data. To get answers about your own bids and account, turn on AI data consent in Preferences & privacy first. You can turn it off at any time.

Talking to a person

Our support team works Monday to Friday, 08:00 to 18:00 UK time. In those hours you can start a live chat with the team. At any other time, leave a message from the same panel and we reply by email.

Reporting a problem well

  1. Choose Report an issue, then Start report.
  2. Say what you were trying to do, what you expected and what happened instead.
  3. Send it. We attach your request ID, the page, your browser, window size and time zone, so support can find your session without asking you for them.

If you reached support from an error page, the request ID from that error is included for you.

Common problems

  • The booking calendar does not load. A browser extension or network block can stop it. Use the link to open the calendar in a new tab.
  • The assistant shows as offline. Email us instead, or report the issue.

articles.title: Find and assess tenders on the Opportunities screen
articles.summary: Search live public tenders, read the match, and decide what to bid for, all from one search bar.
articles.html:
What this is for

The Opportunities screen is where you find public contracts worth bidding for and decide which ones fit your organisation. It is the first step in the find, assess and win journey. You reach it from the Velstrian Bid menu. A tender is a formal invitation from a buyer asking suppliers to bid for a piece of work.

Where the tenders come from

The feed shows live United Kingdom tenders from three public sources: the Find a Tender Service, Contracts Finder, and Public Contracts Scotland. These are the official government channels where public bodies, such as councils, NHS trusts and government departments, must advertise work. There is also an optional SAM.gov source for United States federal opportunities. It uses your own SAM.gov key and has a daily limit, so you turn it on with its source chip, and its results appear in a section of their own that is not scored for relevance.

Step by step

  1. Open Opportunities from the Velstrian Bid menu.
  2. Type what you do into the single search bar at the top, for example "grounds maintenance" or "IT support".
  3. Use the source chips beside the search bar to turn a source on or off.
  4. Read the ranked list. Each result has a relevance score that compares the tender's sector and region with the bids you have recorded, plus its value, so the closest fits sit at the top. Set up tender fit on the same screen and every tender is also scored against what you tell us you bid for.
  5. Save a search so new matching tenders are kept for you. Only a team member who can edit data sees the create and delete controls for saved searches. A viewer sees saved searches but cannot change them.

Assessing a tender before you commit

Opening a result shows the buyer, the contract value, the closing date and the published documents. Use the match position and the deadline together: a strong match with enough time to write a proper response is a better use of your week than a weak match closing in two days. When you decide to go ahead, start a bid from the opportunity and the tender details carry across, so you do not retype them.

What happens next

Starting a bid creates a contract workspace where you upload the tender pack, break it into questions and draft your answers. See the end to end bid workflow guide for the full path from here to a finished submission.

Common problems

Nothing in the feed, or no relevance score: widen your search words, and set up tender fit with the sectors you actually work in, because relevance reads your recorded bids and your tender fit. The private sector note: if your organisation only wins private work, a short note above the feed explains that every source here is a public procurement channel and how private work reaches you instead. If the whole screen sends you back to the Velstrian Bid home, your subscription may be suspended or unpaid, and the home screen shows how to put that right.

articles.title: Reuse your best answers with the Answer library
articles.summary: Keep approved answers in one place and pull them into any bid, so you never rewrite the same thing twice.
articles.html:
What this is for

The Answer library holds answers you have written once and want to reuse. Most tenders ask the same questions in different words, about your quality management, your health and safety, your social value approach and so on. The library lets you store a strong, approved answer and drop it into any future bid, so your team writes less from scratch and keeps a consistent voice.

One library for the whole organisation

This is important. The Answer library belongs to your whole organisation, not to a single bid. An answer you add is available in every bid, and an answer you delete is gone from every future bid, not just the one you are looking at. The screen states this in words, and it sits under the Library area rather than inside any one contract, so the shared scope is clear before you change anything.

Step by step

  1. Open the Answer library from the Velstrian Bid menu.
  2. Read the saved answers. Each one is a reusable block of text you can search.
  3. Add a new answer with your approved wording, so it is ready for the next bid.
  4. Inside a bid, pull a library answer into a question as your starting point, then tailor it to that buyer.

Who can change the library

Everyone on the team can read the library. Adding is open to team members who can edit data. Deleting an answer is limited to the account owner and admins, because a delete removes that answer from every future bid across the organisation. If you do not see a Delete control, your role does not hold that permission, which is working as intended rather than a fault.

What happens next

A tailored library answer still runs through the same review and approval steps as any other answer before you export the submission. Reusing a block is a faster first draft, not a shortcut past review.

Common problems

You cannot delete an answer: that control is owner and admin only, by design. An answer reads oddly in a new bid: the library stores general wording, so always edit a reused answer to name the specific buyer, contract and dates. Treat the library as your source of strong starting points, not as finished answers.

articles.title: Answer the standard selection questions once
articles.summary: Fill in the standard selection questionnaire for your organisation so every future bid starts prefilled.
articles.html:
What this is for

The selection questionnaire, often shortened to SQ, is the standard set of questions a public buyer asks to check a supplier is suitable before looking at the actual bid. It covers things like your finances, your insurance, your relevant experience and whether you have been excluded from public contracts. The questions are much the same from one tender to the next, so Velstrian Bid lets you answer them once for your organisation and reuse them. Private buyers rarely use a standard selection questionnaire, so the tab is shown to organisations that bid for public work. If you bid only for private work you will not see it.

Answered once, prefilled everywhere

Your answers here are your organisation's standing set. They are not tied to any single bid. When you start a bid that includes a suitability stage, these answers are prefilled into it automatically. Editing a bid never changes your standing set, so one bid can never quietly rewrite the answers another bid relies on. For that reason the screen sits under the Library area, beside the Answer library, not inside a contract.

Step by step

  1. Open the Answer library from the Velstrian Bid menu, then its Reusable selection questionnaire tab.
  2. Work down the questions and fill in your organisation's answers.
  3. Where a suggestion appears inside a question, it is drawn from the government Central Digital Platform, the single place suppliers keep their core company details. The suggestion shows its source and has its own accept control, so you choose whether to use it.
  4. Save your answers. They are now ready to prefill your next bid.

Who can edit it

Everyone can read the standing answers. Saving changes is limited to team members who can edit data, so a viewer sees the set without being able to alter it. Because this is organisation wide content, clearing an answer here is not the same as clearing one on a single bid, and the screen says so.

What happens next

Inside a bid with a suitability stage, review the prefilled answers against that specific tender. Some buyers word a question slightly differently or ask for a figure as at a given date, so always check the prefilled text still fits before you submit.

Common problems

A Central Digital Platform suggestion looks wrong: it reflects what is held about your company there, so correct it at source if it is out of date, and accept only what is right. Answers not appearing in a bid: prefill happens for bids that include a suitability stage, so a tender without one will not pull them in.

articles.title: Track buyer changes and clarifications
articles.summary: Find the clarification log and buyer changes in one place, inside the Tender documents of a bid.
articles.html:
What this is for

During a live tender the buyer often issues changes, answers to supplier questions and corrections to the pack. These are called clarifications or addenda. Missing one can mean answering the wrong question or using an old word count, so Velstrian Bid keeps them together where you read the rest of the tender.

Where they live

A clarification answer is a buyer issued change to the tender pack, the same idea as an addendum. For that reason both sit together on the Tender documents screen of a bid, in a section called Changes from the buyer. There is no separate clarifications page any more. An old bookmark or exported link that pointed at a clarifications page now sends you straight to that section, so nothing you saved earlier breaks.

Step by step

  1. Open the bid, then its Tender tab, which opens the Tender documents screen.
  2. Go to the Changes from the buyer section.
  3. Review the buyer changes waiting at the top first, and use the version comparison to see what changed between two versions of a document. Below it, the clarification log holds the questions asked and the answers the buyer gave.
  4. When a change affects a question, update your answer and your compliance checklist for that question.

What happens next

Your drafted answers and your compliance matrix should always reflect the most recent buyer change. Treat a new clarification as a prompt to recheck the rows it touches before you move on.

Why it is kept in one place

Clarifications and addenda used to sit on a page of their own. They now live with the Tender documents because they are the same thing as the pack itself, a set of instructions from the buyer, and reading them apart from the pack made it easy to answer against an out of date version. Keeping them together means the latest wording and the latest rules are always in the same place, which lowers the chance of a mistake that could cost you the bid.

Common problems

You expected a clarifications tab and cannot find one: it was folded into the Tender documents, in Changes from the buyer, on purpose. You cannot add or remove a change: who can write to this section depends on your role, so if the controls are not shown, your role does not hold that permission. A change seems to contradict the original pack: the newest buyer change always wins, so work from the most recent entry and update the affected answers and checklist rows straight away.

articles.title: Automate repeat steps with Workflows
articles.summary: Set up rules that react to events in your workspace, so routine steps happen without a manual nudge.
articles.html:
What this is for

Workflows let you set up rules that run when something happens in Velstrian Tenderworks, so a routine next step does not wait for someone to remember it. A rule has a trigger, the event that starts it, and an action, the thing that then happens. The Workflows screen shows which triggers are available to you and what each one can do, read live from the product rather than from a fixed list.

A plan level feature

Workflows are part of the Integrations capability. They are included on the Portfolio plan, or on the Pro plan with the paid Integrations add on. On any lower plan the Workflows screen shows a locked panel that explains the upgrade rather than controls that could not work. The screen, the behind the scenes service and the application programming interface (the API other software uses) all apply the same rule, so what you see on the page matches what a request would be allowed to do.

Step by step

  1. Open Workflows. It is reached from the Settings area.
  2. If your plan includes it, the builder opens. If not, read the locked panel to see what the upgrade adds.
  3. Choose a trigger from the ones your workspace actually offers.
  4. Choose the action that should follow, then save the rule.

What happens next

Once saved, a rule runs on its own each time its trigger fires. Because the available triggers are read from the product, the list you see is the honest set that can actually fire, rather than a menu of options that quietly do nothing.

Common problems

The builder is locked: your plan does not include Integrations, and the panel explains the Portfolio plan or the Pro add on that unlocks it. Pricing is a question for the account owner through billing, not something stated here. A trigger you expected is missing: only triggers that can genuinely run are offered, so an absent one is not available on your workspace rather than hidden.

articles.title: Connect your other tools with Integrations
articles.summary: Link your customer records and document stores, and send events to tools like Zapier, from one hub.
articles.html:
What this is for

The Integrations hub is where you connect Velstrian Tenderworks to the other tools your organisation already uses, so information moves between them without copy and paste. You reach it from Settings. Like Workflows, Integrations is a plan level capability. It is included on the Portfolio plan and is a paid add on for the Pro plan, and on any other plan the connectors show an honest locked state rather than controls that cannot work.

What you can connect

  • Automation webhooks: send events from Velstrian Tenderworks to automation tools such as Zapier and Make, which can then do the next thing in a tool of your choice. A webhook is just a message your workspace sends to another service when something happens.
  • Customer records, push only: connect a customer relationship management system, HubSpot or Salesforce, using your own account credentials. This connection is push only, so Velstrian Tenderworks sends information out to it and does not read your customer database back in.
  • Document sources, read only: connect a document store, SharePoint, OneDrive or Confluence, again with your own credentials. This connection is read only, so Velstrian Tenderworks can read documents you point it at and does not write back to your store.

Step by step

  1. Open Integrations from Settings.
  2. Pick the connector you want, for example the webhook panel, the customer records panel or the document sources panel.
  3. Follow that connector's steps, supplying your own credentials where it asks for them.
  4. If your plan does not include the connector, read its locked panel to see the plan that adds it.

What happens next

A connected tool keeps working in the background. The direction of each connection is deliberate: customer records go out only, and document sources come in only, so each tool keeps the single job it is built for.

Common problems

A connector is locked: your plan does not include Integrations, and the panel names the plan that unlocks it. Pricing and upgrades are an owner decision through billing. A credential is refused: the customer records and document connectors use your own account's credentials, so check them in the source tool first. Never paste a password or key into a tender answer or any other free text field.

articles.title: Score your suppliers with scorecards
articles.summary: Keep a scored record of how each supplier is performing, opened right inside the supplier's record.
articles.html:
What this is for

A scorecard in Velstrian Buy is a scored record of how a supplier is performing against a contract. It gives buyers, both public bodies and private organisations, a consistent way to measure delivery over time rather than relying on memory or scattered emails. This supports supplier relationship management, the ongoing work of making sure awarded contracts actually deliver.

Where a scorecard lives

A scorecard is a record inside a single supplier's record, not a page of its own in the menu. You open the supplier, go to the scorecards area, and a scorecard opens as a panel over that view. This keeps every score attached to the right supplier, so you always know whose performance you are reading. You only ever see suppliers that belong to your own organisation.

Step by step

  1. Open Velstrian Buy and go to your suppliers.
  2. Open the supplier you want to score.
  3. Go to the Scorecards area for that supplier.
  4. Open or create a scorecard. It appears as a panel over the supplier record, so the supplier stays in view behind it.
  5. Record your scores, then close the panel to return to the supplier record.

What happens next

Scores build up over time into a performance history you can revisit before a renewal, a review meeting or an award decision on future work. Scorecards sit alongside the other parts of a supplier record, such as reviews, risks and commitments, so one supplier record holds the full picture.

Why score at all

Scoring a supplier turns vague impressions into a record you can act on. A low score on one measure is an early warning you can raise at the next review, before it becomes a bigger problem. A steady run of strong scores is evidence you can point to when deciding whether to extend a contract or award the supplier new work. For public buyers this also helps show that spending is being managed and that decisions about suppliers rest on recorded performance rather than memory.

Common problems

A supplier is not listed: you only see suppliers that belong to your organisation, so a supplier added under another organisation will not appear. The scorecard opens as a panel, not a full page: that is intended, so the supplier context stays visible behind it. You cannot find an old score: scorecards are kept inside the supplier record, so open the supplier first and then its Scorecards area rather than searching for the score on its own.

articles.title: Run a supplier review
articles.summary: Hold a structured review of a supplier and keep the record attached to that supplier.
articles.html:
What this is for

A supplier review in Velstrian Buy is a structured check in on how a supplier is doing, held at set points during a contract. Regular reviews are a core part of supplier relationship management, the work of keeping an awarded contract on track. They give both public and private buyers an agreed moment to look at performance, raise concerns and agree what happens next.

Where a review lives

A review session is a record inside a single supplier's record, not a separate screen in the menu. You open the supplier, go to the reviews area, and a review session opens on that view. Keeping the review attached to the supplier means the discussion, and anything agreed in it, stays with the right contract rather than drifting into a general notes pile. You only see suppliers belonging to your own organisation.

Step by step

  1. Open Velstrian Buy and go to your suppliers.
  2. Open the supplier you want to review.
  3. Go to the Reviews area for that supplier.
  4. Open or start a review session. It opens on the supplier record, so the supplier stays in context.
  5. Work through the review and record the outcome, then close the session.

What happens next

A completed review becomes part of the supplier's history, alongside scorecards, risks and commitments. Over several reviews you build a clear record of how the relationship has gone, which helps at renewal time or when deciding future work.

Reviews and scorecards together

A review is the conversation, and a scorecard is the measure. Used together they give a rounded view: the scorecard shows how the numbers moved, and the review captures why and what you agreed to do about it. Holding both inside the same supplier record means you are never hunting across different parts of the product to prepare for a meeting, and the full story of a contract stays in one place from award to renewal.

Common problems

A review will not open for a supplier that is not yours: each session is checked against the supplier it belongs to, so you cannot open one for a supplier outside your organisation. A review opens on the supplier record rather than as its own page: that is by design, to keep the review tied to the supplier. You cannot find a past review: open the supplier first, then its Reviews area, because reviews are stored inside the supplier record rather than in a separate list.

articles.title: Track delivered value with the Value tracker
articles.summary: Keep sight of the value a contract is actually delivering, with a finance view for sign off.
articles.html:
What this is for

The Value tracker in Velstrian Buy helps a buying organisation keep sight of the value a contract is actually delivering after award, not just what was promised in the bid. It is built with finance in mind, so a chief finance officer or a budget holder can see delivered value in one place. This matters for both public spending, where value for money must be shown, and private budgets.

Step by step

  1. Open Velstrian Buy.
  2. Open Reporting, then its Value tracker tab.
  3. Review the totals and the items waiting for a finance decision.
  4. Work through the queue, confirming or questioning each item as your process requires.

How the figures are kept honest

The tracker is deliberately careful with its numbers. The finance totals it shows are kept separate and are not quietly recombined into a single headline figure, so a reader always knows which total they are looking at. This keeps a delivered value figure from being confused with a forecast or a target.

What happens next

Confirmed value becomes part of the record you can show at a budget review or an audit. Used alongside scorecards and reviews, the Value tracker turns a promise made at bid time into evidence of what the contract delivered.

Why it is kept separate from the bid

Value promised in a bid and value actually delivered are two different things, and treating them as the same is how a contract quietly underperforms without anyone noticing. The Value tracker keeps the delivered figure distinct, so a confident claim made at bid time is checked against what really happened. A finance queue puts the confirming step with the person who owns the budget, rather than leaving it to whoever happened to run the contract, which keeps the sign off honest.

Common problems

The screen is not available: the Value tracker is a Velstrian Buy feature, so access depends on your product entitlement, and if it is not granted you are returned to the Velstrian Buy area. Two totals do not add up to one number: that is on purpose, because the tracker keeps those totals apart rather than merging them. An item is stuck in the queue: it is waiting for a finance decision, so it stays there until someone with that responsibility confirms or questions it.

articles.title: Plan work with the buyer pipeline and contract register
articles.summary: See your upcoming and current contracts in one pipeline, with the publication views public buyers need.
articles.html:
What this is for

The buyer pipeline in Velstrian Buy gives a buying organisation one view of its upcoming and current contracts, so planning does not live in a spreadsheet. It works for public and private buyers alike. Public buyers also have publication duties under the Procurement Act 2023, and the pipeline holds the view that supports them, so planning and transparency share one source of truth. A private buyer sees that same view written as a plain forward plan for suppliers.

The views it holds

The pipeline screen shows one job at a time, chosen by a view control, with the pipeline itself as the default. The other views read from the same data. Pipeline notice holds the content a pipeline notice needs (Procurement Act 2023, section 93 (pipeline notices)), and Document packs builds board, committee and business case packs from your own records. The contract register, with its download, sits on the Contracts screen beside the contracts it lists. Because they all read from one place, the planning list and the published views cannot drift apart.

Step by step

  1. Open Velstrian Buy, then Requirements, then its Pipeline tab.
  2. Use the view control near the top to switch between Pipeline, Pipeline notice and Document packs.
  3. Open a row to work on that requirement. A quick request for quotes row opens on the Quick RFQ screen rather than as a full requirement pack.
  4. When you need the contract register for publication or reporting, open Contracts and choose Download contract register.

What happens next

A planned item in the pipeline becomes a requirement you take out to suppliers, then an evaluation, then an awarded contract you manage. The pipeline is the planning end of that journey, and the contract register is the published record at the other end.

Common problems

You can only see one view at a time: that is deliberate, so switch views with the control rather than looking for them side by side. The contract register is not one of the views: it is on the Contracts screen. A pipeline row opens somewhere unexpected: a quick request for quotes opens on its own Quick RFQ screen, which is intended, because it is a lighter process than a full requirement.

articles.title: Run a call-off from a framework
articles.summary: Start a bid as a call-off under a framework your organisation already holds a place on, scored lot by lot.
articles.html:
What this is for

A framework agreement is a pre approved list of suppliers that a buyer can draw from without running a whole new tender each time. A dynamic purchasing system, or DPS, works in a similar way. Awarding a specific piece of work from a framework is called a call-off. If your organisation holds a place on a framework, Velstrian Bid lets you start a call-off bid under it, so you answer only what the call-off asks rather than proving your suitability again.

Where it starts

Frameworks are mostly a public sector route, so the call-off option is offered when the bid is for a public buyer. A bid for a private buyer shows a short note explaining which start options do not apply to it. The framework positions your organisation holds are listed on the Frameworks and lots screen. An owner or administrator records each position, the framework and the lot you hold a place on, in your bid profile, and it then appears there ready to use.

Step by step

  1. Open Start a bid from the Velstrian Bid menu.
  2. Under the other ways to start, choose Start a call-off. This opens Frameworks and lots.
  3. Find the framework position the call-off is under and choose Start a call-off beside it.
  4. Say how the call-off is being awarded, by mini competition or by direct award. Selection is not asked again, because you passed it when you joined the framework.
  5. Draft, review and export as you would for any bid. A framework split into lots is scored lot by lot.

What happens next

A call-off creates a bid workspace like any other, so the drafting, review and export steps are the same. Only the call-off quality answers need evidence, because your selection evidence is already lodged with the framework. Working lot by lot keeps each parcel of work clear, which matters when you bid for some lots and not others.

Common problems

You cannot see Start a call-off: it is offered for bids to a public buyer, so check the buyer type you chose. Frameworks and lots is empty: no position has been recorded yet, so ask an owner or administrator to add the framework and lot in your bid profile. Lots are confusing: treat each lot as its own small bid with its own answers, which is how the call-off is scored.

articles.title: Keep a consistent brand voice
articles.summary: Set your organisation's writing voice once so drafted answers sound like you, with an optional voice for a sector.
articles.html:
What this is for

Your brand voice is the way your organisation writes: formal or warm, brief or detailed, plain or technical. Velstrian Bid lets you set that voice once so the answers it drafts sound like you, rather than generic. A consistent voice across a long bid reads as more professional and is easier for an evaluator to follow.

One voice for the organisation

Your brand voice belongs to the whole organisation, not to a single bid, so it sits in the Library beside the Answer library rather than inside a contract. You can keep one default voice for all sectors and add a voice for a particular sector, which is useful if you bid into markets that expect a different tone, for example a technical sector against a community facing one. The screen shows which voice would write the next answer, so you always know which one is in use.

Step by step

  1. Open the Answer library from the Velstrian Bid menu, then its Brand voice tab.
  2. Choose Define a voice and give it a name your team will recognise.
  3. Leave the sector as all sectors for your default voice, or pick a sector for a voice that applies only there.
  4. Write the guidance on how you write. You can start from an answer that won and have the guidance drafted from it, then check it before you save. A sample of your writing is optional.
  5. Choose Save and use.

What happens next

When Velstrian Bid drafts an answer, it uses the voice in use as a guide, so the first draft already sounds closer to your own writing. A writing sample is read only for style, such as sentence length and spelling convention, and its facts are never reused. You still edit every answer, and the voice is a starting point, not a replacement for your judgement.

Why a saved voice helps

Without a saved voice, each drafted answer starts from a neutral tone, and a long bid can end up reading as if several different people wrote it. That costs you time, because you then rewrite for tone on top of rewriting for content. A saved voice moves that work up front and does it once. It also helps a new team member write in a way that matches the rest of the organisation, rather than guessing the house style.

Common problems

A draft still does not sound right: make the guidance clearer about the tone you want, and remember you always edit the draft. You bid into very different markets: add a voice for a sector rather than forcing one voice to cover them all. A voice is saved but not in use: open it, choose to use it for new answers, and save.

articles.title: Use the API and webhooks
articles.summary: Create API keys and webhook endpoints to connect Velstrian Tenderworks to your own systems, and see delivery history.
articles.html:
What this is for

The API and webhooks screen is for connecting Velstrian Tenderworks to your own software. An API key lets your systems read or write through the application programming interface, the controlled way one program talks to another. A webhook is a message Velstrian Tenderworks sends to a web address you choose when something happens, so your systems can react. The screen also shows delivery history, a log of the webhook messages that were sent and whether they arrived.

A plan level feature with a permission

API access is part of the Integrations capability. It is included on the Portfolio plan and is a paid add on for the Pro plan. On a plan without it, the API keys section shows a locked state that explains the upgrade, while the delivery history stays visible. Managing webhook endpoints also needs the manage integrations permission, so a team member without it can look but not change. Pricing and upgrades are an owner decision through billing.

Step by step

  1. Open Settings, then API & webhooks.
  2. In the endpoints section, add a webhook endpoint, the web address that should receive messages.
  3. Create an API key for your systems if your plan includes it. Give it a name and only the scopes it needs. The key is shown once, so copy it then and store it safely. Treat it like a password and never paste it into a tender answer or any shared document.
  4. Use the deliveries section to check what was sent and whether it succeeded.

What happens next

Once an endpoint is set up, Velstrian Tenderworks sends it a message each time the matching event happens, and the delivery history records the result. If a delivery fails, the history is where you see it. The same screen links to the API documentation, which lists every endpoint and how to sign in to it.

Common problems

The API keys section is locked: your plan does not include Integrations, and the panel names the plan that unlocks it. You cannot add an endpoint: that needs the manage integrations permission, so ask an owner or admin. A key has been lost: keys are shown only once, so revoke the old key and create a new one.

articles.title: Read your win and loss insights
articles.summary: See how your bids are going over a period you choose, with the reasons behind wins and losses and what bids cost you.
articles.html:
What this is for

Insights shows how your bids are doing over time. It reads your own bid records and presents them, so you can see a pattern rather than judging one bid at a time. It covers the reasons behind wins and losses and a bid cost retrospective, which looks back at what bids cost you to produce from the rate cards and effort you recorded.

A reading screen

Insights reads your data, it does not produce documents. Each figure is read for the period it covers, so a figure from one quarter is never mistaken for an all time figure. The full Insights view is part of the Pro plan of Velstrian Bid and above. On a lower plan the rest of the screen shows its upgrade lock, and the win and loss insights and the bid cost retrospective stay open to you below it.

Step by step

  1. Open Insights from the Velstrian Bid menu.
  2. Read the win and loss section to see how recent bids have gone and why.
  3. Read the bid cost retrospective to see what bids cost to produce.
  4. Check the period each figure covers, so you compare like with like.

What happens next

Use the patterns to decide where to spend your bidding effort. If a type of work loses more often, Insights helps you see it early. To produce a document rather than read a trend, use the Bid reports tab beside Insights.

How to read it well

Insights is most useful when you look at the shape rather than any single number. A run of losses in one kind of work, or a rising cost to produce certain bids, is a signal worth acting on. Because every figure carries the period it covers, you can compare one window against another on a fair footing, instead of comparing a busy quarter with a quiet one. Treat the cost retrospective as a prompt to check whether a type of bid is worth the effort it takes, not as a verdict on any one person.

Common problems

Part of Insights is locked: the full view needs the Pro plan, and the lock names the plan that opens it. A figure looks low or high: read the period it covers before you act on it. The numbers feel thin: Insights reads your own bid records, so the more of your bidding runs through Velstrian Bid, and the more outcomes and costs you record, the fuller the picture becomes.

articles.title: Produce bid reports and a board summary
articles.summary: Run a report on your bids from a catalogue of templates, export it, or have it emailed on a schedule.
articles.html:
What this is for

Bid reports is where you produce documents from your bid data. Where Insights reads a trend on screen, Bid reports makes a file you can share, for example with your board or a client. It is a catalogue of report templates, led by the Board executive summary. You can run a report, export it, or have it emailed on a schedule.

A catalogue, not a list

The report cards are drawn from the registered catalogue of templates, so the screen only offers a report the system can actually produce. The Board executive summary comes first, then the other templates. The monthly report for a single bid is not in this catalogue, because it belongs to that bid.

Step by step

  1. Open Insights from the Velstrian Bid menu, then its Bid reports tab.
  2. Choose a report from the catalogue, starting with the Board executive summary if you need an overview.
  3. Download it, or set it to be emailed on a schedule.
  4. For a single bid's monthly report, open that bid and go to its Contract delivery tab, where the monthly reports sit once the bid is in delivery.

What happens next

A produced report is a document you own and can send on. For a live view of performance rather than a document, use Insights. The two are deliberately split: Insights reads, Bid reports produces.

When to use a report instead of Insights

Reach for Bid reports when someone outside the screen needs the information: a board that wants a summary before a meeting, or a client that wants a written update. Reach for Insights when you are the reader and you want to see a trend live. The Board executive summary is the quickest way to an overview document, because it gathers the headline picture into one file. The monthly report for a bid answers a narrower question, how that contract is being delivered, which is why it sits on the bid rather than in the shared catalogue.

Common problems

A report you expected is missing: the catalogue only shows templates the system can produce, so an absent one is not available rather than hidden. You cannot find a bid's monthly report here: it is on that bid's Contract delivery tab. The page says your account is not linked to an organisation: reports run on an organisation's bids, so join or create one first. You wanted a live view, not a file: that is Insights.

articles.title: Get set up when you first sign in
articles.summary: The short setup journey that confirms your organisation, how you work with tenders and the products you will use.
articles.html:
What this is for

When you first sign in to Velstrian Tenderworks, a short setup journey gets your workspace ready. It confirms who your organisation is, how you work with tenders and which products you will use, so the rest of the product is shaped to your situation from the start. It is a few screens, not a long form, and a progress bar shows how far through you are.

Confirm your organisation type

One screen asks you to confirm your organisation type. Velstrian Tenderworks makes a starting guess from the ending of the address you signed in with and pre-selects it, and says plainly that it is an assumption, not your answer. You check it, change it if it is wrong, then tick the box to confirm it is the right description of your organisation. You cannot carry on until you confirm, so the type recorded is always one you agreed.

Choose your products

If your organisation holds both Velstrian Bid and Velstrian Buy, a later screen lets you set each one up. If you hold only one product, you do not see this screen. The setup cards follow what your organisation actually holds, so a product you do not have is never offered.

Step by step

  1. Sign in for the first time. The setup journey opens on its own.
  2. Check your organisation name and confirm your organisation type.
  3. Say how you work with tenders: We answer tenders if you are a supplier, or We run tenders if you buy.
  4. Say where you trade, and set up the product or products you hold if asked.
  5. Choose Finish setup. If you need to stop part way, choose Finish later.

Why the setup is short on purpose

The journey asks only for what shapes the rest of the product: who you are and what you will use. Everything else, your organisation profile, your evidence, your team, is set up later in the product where it has more room and more context. Keeping the first run short means you reach a working workspace quickly. Confirming the organisation type early also means the help, the examples and the defaults you meet afterwards already fit a buyer or a supplier, public or private.

Common problems

The suggested organisation type is wrong: change it before you confirm. You did not see a product choice screen: that screen appears only when you hold both products. You want to change something set here later: finish the short journey first and adjust it from Settings afterwards.

articles.title: Your Home screen and the Action centre
articles.summary: See what needs you first, what is in progress and where to go next, then open the full list in the Action centre.
articles.html:
What this is for

Home is the first screen you see after you sign in to Velstrian Tenderworks. It answers one question: what do I do next? The Action centre is the longer list behind it. Together they work for a supplier answering tenders, a buyer running them and a firm doing both, for public and private work alike.

What you see on Home

A short greeting comes first, then a queue headed by how many things need you, for example that one thing needs you before a date. The items are numbered and the first is the most pressing. Each card has one next step, so you never have to decide where to start.

Below the queue sit your work in progress, with a link to open your bids and, if you buy, your buyer requirements. Further down are quick actions for your product, the products you hold and a list of recent changes with a link to your notifications. If you are new, a short getting started list takes the place of the queue and shows how far through setup you are.

How the queue is ordered

The order follows fixed rules, the same on every visit. Anything blocking your account comes first, then legal deadlines, then money at risk, then everyday work. Overdue items and items due this week come before later dates, and quicker tasks rise when two items are otherwise equal. Open the small note that asks how the queue is ordered to read the rules on screen.

Step by step

  1. Open Home from the menu.
  2. Read the headline. If it says you are all caught up, nothing is waiting on you.
  3. Start with number one and use the single next step on its card.
  4. Snooze an item that is not blocking you if it can wait. A snoozed item with a deadline comes back no later than a week before that deadline.
  5. Choose View all in Action centre to see everything.

The Action centre

The Action centre shows everything that needs you across your products, ordered by how soon it is due. Nothing is hidden there, so items you snoozed on Home still appear, marked with a badge. You can search by title, detail or product, filter by when something is due (overdue, due soon, upcoming, later or no date), filter by product, and switch between priority order and soonest due date first. The snooze control lives on Home, because the Action centre is a read only view.

If it goes wrong

If part of your work could not be read, the page says it could not check everything and offers a retry. Nothing has been changed or lost, and the list may simply be incomplete until you try again. An empty Action centre is good news. It reads that you are all caught up, and it offers a shortcut to start a bid or create a requirement. If a filter shows nothing, the page says the filters are the reason and offers to show everything again.

articles.title: Ask the AI compliance advisor
articles.summary: Open the assistant from any screen and ask about the procurement rules your products cover, with the sources it used shown under every answer.
articles.html:
What this is for

The AI compliance advisor answers questions about the procurement and social value rules that Velstrian Bid and Velstrian Buy cover. Use it when you want a plain explanation of a rule, for example when a social value weighting applies or what a carbon reduction plan has to contain. It is built for people who are not procurement specialists, so ask in everyday words.

Where to find it

The advisor is part of the one assistant panel that opens on top of whatever screen you are on, so you never lose your place. Choose Compliance advisor from the menu to open the panel in its AI mode. An older advisor link still works, and it takes you back to the screen you came from with the panel open. If your organisation holds neither product, the advisor asks you to add one first and offers a link to browse products.

Step by step

  1. Choose Compliance advisor from the menu.
  2. Type your question in the box, or pick one of the suggested questions.
  3. Read the answer. The sources it relied on are listed under it, with a link when there is a verified official page.
  4. Ask a follow up in the same conversation.
  5. Choose Stop if you want to end an answer early. Your question stays on screen so you can ask it again.

What it knows and what it does not

The advisor is grounded in published United Kingdom procurement and social value rules. Its opening panel tells you which rules it covers for your organisation. For a buyer it explains what to require of bidders and how to evaluate it. For a firm that so far bids only for private work, it says that these rules govern public procurement and will apply when you bid for public work.

By default the advisor does not read your own bids, evidence or uploaded documents. If you turn on AI data consent in your privacy settings, it can also read your contract details, your social value commitments and counts of your evidence, plus the confirmed requirements of a bid you select. It never opens your evidence files. You can turn the consent off again at any time.

If it goes wrong

If an answer says no source document was matched, treat it as a lead and check the official guidance before you rely on it. An answer is advice to help you decide, not legal advice. If a conversation you reopen from history shows no sources, that is expected, because history does not store them. For a question about how to use the product itself, the support assistant on the Support page is the better place.

articles.title: See who won public contracts, and when the work returns
articles.summary: Search recent public award notices, read what a buyer has done before and spot contracts that are coming back to market.
articles.html:
What this is for

The Awards and incumbents screen shows who won recently published United Kingdom public contracts, what value the notice stated and, where the notice says so, when the winner's contract ends and the work is likely to be bought again. It helps you choose which public tenders are worth your time and who you will be up against. It covers public contracts only. If your organisation has never bid for a public buyer, the tab is hidden, and the page is still there if you open its link. Private work has no public award notices, so for private buyers you use your own research.

Where to find it

Open Opportunities in the Velstrian Bid menu and choose the Awards and incumbents tab.

Step by step

  1. Open the Awards and incumbents tab.
  2. Narrow the list by winning supplier, by the buyer that awarded the contract, or by how recently the notice was published. Buyers from your own bids are offered beside the buyer filter. Choosing one fills the field and nothing is filled for you. Results update as you change a filter.
  3. Read each record: who won, who awarded it, the stated value, how many bids were received, and when the contract starts and ends.
  4. Open the award notice to read the original.
  5. Open What a buyer has done before and type a buyer's name to see how many firms bid, how often small firms won, who holds the work now and when it ends.

Reading the numbers honestly

The screen never invents a figure. If a notice stated no value, it says not published, which means unknown and not zero. If a notice did not say how many bids it received, that does not mean nobody bid. The returns to market date is the buyer's own published end date, not a forecast, and contracts are often extended. The buyer figures are counts of past notices, so they show what happened and not what comes next. A buyer with only a few notices is flagged as a hint rather than a pattern.

Coverage and renewals

You can open a coverage panel to see which publishing portals feed the list. Read results as covering those portals only. An empty result means no matching notice in the covered feeds, not that no contract was awarded. A renewals section may also appear lower down. If it shows a padlock, it is not part of your current plan, and Billing in Settings shows what each plan includes.

If it goes wrong

If the page says award history is not included in your plan, see Billing. If it says the history could not be loaded, choose try again. If a name search finds nothing, check the spelling against the name on the notice.

articles.title: Choose which alerts and emails you get
articles.summary: Find your notification history and set which reminders, team alerts and update emails reach you.
articles.html:
What this is for

Velstrian Tenderworks tells you about things that matter, such as a bid deadline getting close, a colleague mentioning you or a reviewer asking for changes. You choose which of these reach your inbox. Email is the only channel used for these alerts today.

Your notification history

The recent changes list on Home and the notification bell in the header lead to your notification history, where you can look back at what happened and when. Use it when you missed an email or want to find a change someone made.

Step by step

  1. Open Settings, then Notifications.
  2. Work down the four groups. Switch each alert on or off with its toggle.
  3. Choose how often you want email, if your plan offers a frequency choice.
  4. Check that the page says all changes saved. Changes save by themselves, with no save button.

The four groups

  • Deadlines and reminders keep a bid moving before its submission date. They cover the bid deadline reminder, the monthly evidence reminder for active contracts and the getting started nudges, such as a reminder that you have not uploaded a tender yet.
  • Team activity sends an email when you are mentioned, replied to or given a question to answer, and when a reviewer signs off, asks for changes or rejects your work.
  • Updates and reports covers changes to procurement rules that affect your bids, the reports you have scheduled by email, and tips and product news. You can switch off the tips and news and still receive emails about your account and billing.
  • Security emails, such as a new sign in or a password change, are always on to protect your account and cannot be switched off.

Good to know

Alerts follow the products you hold. The same settings apply whether your work is public or private. If a setting shows coming soon, it is not live yet and nothing is sent for it. If a setting shows an upgrade note, the choice belongs to a larger plan.

If it goes wrong

If the page says it could not load your preferences, it shows none on purpose, because defaults would not be yours. Your saved settings are unchanged and editing stays off until the page loads, so reload it. If a change could not be saved, the page says so and offers a retry, and your other settings stay as they were. If an email you expect never arrives, check the alert is switched on, check your spam folder and look at the address on your profile.

articles.title: Set up your profile, currency and how the app looks
articles.summary: Change your name, photo and sign in email, pick your currency, and choose a light or dark theme, colour palette and time zone.
articles.html:
What this is for

Two settings pages shape Velstrian Tenderworks for you alone. Profile holds details about you. Appearance holds how the app looks and how it shows dates and times. Neither changes anything for your colleagues.

Your profile

  1. Open Settings, then Profile.
  2. Check your name and job title. A name is required.
  3. Add or change your profile photo. You can crop it before you save. If you remove it, your initials show instead and you must upload the photo again to bring it back.
  4. Choose your currency. It is used for indicative figures across the product, for private and public work alike. Billing is always invoiced in pounds sterling whatever you choose.
  5. To change your sign in email, use the email form on the page. Your current address keeps working until you confirm the new one.

Appearance

  1. Open Settings, then Appearance.
  2. Pick a theme: System follows your device, Light is always light and Dark is always dark. The change shows straight away.
  3. Pick a colour palette. Each palette has a light and a dark version, and the theme chooses between them. Your choice is saved to your account, so it follows you to every device you sign in on.
  4. Under Display, check your time zone. The page offers the one your browser reports, and you can pick another.

Why the time zone matters

Deadlines, reminders and recent changes are shown in your time zone. A wrong time zone makes a deadline look an hour or more earlier or later than it is, which matters when a tender closes at a set time. Set it once and check it after you travel.

If it goes wrong

If a change on Appearance could not be saved to your account, the page says it was applied on this device only and offers a retry. If your saved time zone could not be read, the page says so and pauses the control until you reload. If the profile page says it could not save, check that your name is filled in and try again. The details of your organisation, such as its name and type, are changed in the organisation settings by an owner or an admin, not here.

articles.title: Download a copy of your data
articles.summary: Ask for a portable copy of the records held on your account and collect the private download link from your email.
articles.html:
What this is for

You are entitled to a portable copy of the personal records held about you. The Your data page prepares one for you. The copy covers your profile, the organisations you belong to, your contracts and bids, your history of AI use, your billing records and your audit log. It is the same whether your work is public or private.

Where to find it

Open Settings, then Sign-in and security, and choose the link to request a data export. The page is called Your data.

Step by step

  1. Open the Your data page.
  2. Choose Request export.
  3. If asked, confirm that it is you with your second factor. If you have not set one up yet, you are guided through it, which takes about a minute, and you come straight back to the page.
  4. Wait for the export to be prepared. This usually takes a few minutes. The page updates by itself and an email tells you when it is ready.
  5. Open the email, or return to the page, and choose Download beside the export in your history.

Good to know

The download link is private to you and expires after a few days, so download it soon. The page lists every export you have requested with its status: pending, processing, ready to download, link expired or failed. You can ask for one export at a time, and after one completes there is a waiting period before you can ask for the next. The page tells you the date you can request again.

If it goes wrong

If the button says an export is already in progress, wait for it to finish. If a request has run for over an hour, the page says it is taking longer than expected and lets you start a new one. If an export shows failed, start a new one, and contact support from the Support page if it fails again. If a link has expired, request a new export. If the history cannot be loaded, the page says it is a temporary problem and does not mean you have no exports.

articles.title: Report on your contracts: Reporting, Award record and supplier feedback
articles.summary: Download branded reports, track committed against delivered value, export your award record and ask suppliers to rate the working relationship.
articles.html:
What this is for

Reporting is where a buyer shows what has been bought and what it has delivered, to a board, an auditor or a funder. It works for public bodies and for private companies, and the wording follows your organisation type. It sits in the Velstrian Buy menu and has tabs for the portfolio view, the award record, the value tracker and supplier feedback. The value tracker has its own guide.

The reports and exports

The reports view starts with an at a glance count of your requirements, contracts and suppliers. Below it, an Exports section offers branded reports you can download and send on, and a Live surfaces section links to the portfolio and award record views.

The Portfolio tab

This tab shows committed against delivered social value across all your contracts, by theme, as a chart you can also read as a table. Each theme is marked on track, at risk, not yet due or breached, and under delivery alerts are worked out from your own records. If no commitments are recorded yet, the page is empty and offers a shortcut to your contracts. Add commitments to an awarded contract and they appear here.

The Award record tab

Every contract you award adds one row. The tab totals the notices and their value and exports to CSV, PDF and Word. For a contracting authority it presents the award notices that the Procurement Act 2023 requires. For a private company it is simply your own record of awards for your files, your board or an audit, and it says the statutory duty does not reach you.

The Relationship feedback tab

Here suppliers rate the working relationship with you. You choose a contract and a quarter and enter the supplier contact's email. The supplier receives a single use link, and the page lists the links you have sent and whether each still works. Answers stay private. You see how many suppliers answered, never who gave which score, and an average is published only after the quarter closes and enough different suppliers have answered.

Step by step

  1. Open Reporting from the Velstrian Buy menu.
  2. Download the report you need from Exports.
  3. Open the Award record tab and export it in the format your reader wants.
  4. Open Relationship feedback, choose a contract and a quarter, enter the supplier contact's email and choose Email the rating link.

If it goes wrong

If a tab cannot load, choose try again. Nothing is changed by a failed load. If you cannot ask a supplier for a rating, the contract needs a supplier recorded first. If the email is on your own organisation's domain, the page warns you, because a rating is meant for the supplier and not a colleague. If a rating link email fails to send, check the address and send again.
